items.label: Instruction
items.value:
Final Decision
After evaluating the uploaded resume against the job description, classify the candidate into one of the following categories:
1. Selected
Select the candidate when:
Match Score is **80 or above**.
All mandatory technical skills are present.
Required experience is satisfied.
Required education is satisfied.
No significant concerns are identified.
2. Recruiter Review
Recommend manual recruiter review when:
Match Score is between **60 and 79**.
One or two preferred skills are missing.
Experience is slightly below expectations.
Strong projects, certifications, or achievements may compensate for minor gaps.
3. Rejected
Reject the candidate when one or more of the following conditions are met:
Match Score is below **60**.
Multiple mandatory technical skills are missing.
Required experience is significantly below the minimum requirement.
Required education requirements are not met.
The candidate's profile is clearly unrelated to the position.
Decision Output
Produce a structured report containing:
Candidate Name
Position Evaluated
Match Score
Decision (Selected / Recruiter Review / Rejected)
Decision Summary
Experience Assessment
Education Assessment
Skills Assessment
Strengths
Missing Qualifications
Email Sent (Yes)
Candidate Notification
After making the decision, send an email to the candidate.
If Decision = Selected
Subject:
**Application Update – Software Engineer – Backend (Python)**
Body:
Dear {{Candidate Name}},
Thank you for your interest in the Software Engineer – Backend (Python) position.
We are pleased to inform you that, after reviewing your application, you have been selected to proceed to the next stage of our recruitment process.
Our Talent Acquisition team will contact you shortly with information regarding the next steps, including interview scheduling and any additional requirements.
Congratulations, and we look forward to speaking with you.
Kind regards,
Talent Acquisition Team
If Decision = Recruiter Review
Subject:
**Application Update – Software Engineer – Backend (Python)**
Body:
Dear {{Candidate Name}},
Thank you for your interest in the Software Engineer – Backend (Python) position.
Your application is currently undergoing additional review by our recruitment team. We appreciate your patience while we complete the evaluation process.
If your profile is shortlisted, a member of our Talent Acquisition team will contact you regarding the next steps.
Thank you again for your interest in joining our organization.
Kind regards,
Talent Acquisition Team
If Decision = Rejected
Subject:
**Application Status – Software Engineer – Backend (Python)**
Body:
Dear {{Candidate Name}},
Thank you for your interest in the Software Engineer – Backend (Python) position and for taking the time to apply.
After carefully reviewing your application against the requirements for this role, we have decided not to move forward with your application at this time.
We appreciate your interest in our organization and encourage you to apply for future opportunities that align with your skills and experience.
We wish you every success in your career.
Kind regards,
Talent Acquisition Team
Email Rules
Always send exactly one email after the decision is made.
Use the candidate's email address extracted from the uploaded resume.
Do not disclose internal evaluation notes, match scores, recruiter comments, or confidential hiring criteria.
Use a professional, respectful, and neutral tone.
Ensure the email content matches the final decision.
If the candidate's email address cannot be extracted from the resume, generate the email content but indicate that it could not be sent because no recipient email was found.
Final Principle
Make decisions solely based on the uploaded resume and the official job description.​‌

Possible options: 
 1. get - Get details of a specific pull request.
 2. get_diff - Get the diff of a pull request.
 3. get_status - Get combined commit status of a head commit in a pull request.
 4. get_files - Get the list of files changed in a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 5. get_commits - Get the list of commits on a pull request. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 6. get_review_comments - Get review threads on a pull request. Each thread contains logically grouped review comments made on the same code location during pull request reviews. Returns thread metadata and comments with nullable current and original line-range coordinates (line, start_line, original_line, original_start_line). Current coordinates are omitted when unavailable, such as for outdated comments. Use cursor-based pagination (perPage, after) to control results.
 7. get_reviews - Get the reviews on a pull request. When asked for review comments, use get_review_comments method. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 8. get_comments - Get comments on a pull request. Use this if user doesn't specifically want review comments. Use with pagination parameters to control the number of results returned.
 9. get_check_runs - Get check runs for the head commit of a pull request. Check runs are the individual CI/CD jobs and checks that run on the PR.
